projects.title: Evaluation Frameworks for Autonomous Scientific Research

review.alternative: Standard utility maximization with biased priors might account for the observed polarization.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence demonstrating that resource rationality naturally predicts belief polarization without auxiliary assumptions.

claims.statement: Resource rationality frameworks encounter empirical phenomena such as belief polarization and the size-weight illusion that are not readily explained by standard performance- or resource-based constraints.

support.explanation: Identifies limitations in standard resource rationality models when explaining specific cognitive biases and illusions.
support.passage: We present two phenomena – belief polarization and the size-weight illusion – that are not obviously explained by performance- or resource-based constraints, nor by the authors’ brief discussion of reference repulsion. Can resource rationality accommodate them?

actions.findings: Resource rationality frameworks encounter empirical phenomena such as belief polarization and the size-weight illusion that are not readily explained by standard performance- or resource-based constraints. [source-30ec9be110ec4599]
actions.limitations: The integration of physical error correction with cognitive epistemological models remains theoretical, and resource rationality accounts for biases are still under active investigation.
actions.next_questions: How can autonomous systems incorporate resource-rational constraints to avoid systematic belief polarization?
actions.reason: Revise notebook findings using newly collected evidence on resource rationality and cognitive biases.
actions.summary: Resource rationality models must account for anomalies like belief polarization and weight illusions that extend beyond standard performance- or resource-based optimization constraints.
actions.title: Metareasoning and Robustness in Rational Agency

actions.assumptions_changed: Assumption that all cognitive deviations are simple resource-allocation limits.
actions.new_frame: Metareasoning and self-correction must account for non-resource-rational cognitive biases and belief polarization.
actions.old_frame: Metareasoning relies purely on static optimization of planning versus execution.
actions.reason: Reframe the project approach to integrate findings on belief polarization and resource rationality.
actions.strategy: Expand assumption testing to cover systematic cognitive biases.
actions.trigger: Incorporation of new evidence on resource rationality limits.
